title: Two polite algorithms once made each other wait
body: Nagle's algorithm holds small packets hoping to batch them, while delayed ACK holds acknowledgements hoping to piggyback; together they can stall each other for tens of milliseconds per exchange. Telnet-era optimisations colliding in modern RPC is a classic latency mystery. Disabling Nagle with TCP_NODELAY is the traditional exorcism, with its own packet-rate costs.
